newsitem.title: FRANCE: Grenade hits police barracks in southern Corsica.
newsitem.headline: Grenade hits police barracks in southern Corsica.

text.p: A grenade blast hit a police barracks in the southern Corsican town of Figari early on Thursday, causing minor damage but no injuries, police said.
A few hours earlier a bomb hit a local office of the Renault automaking firm, damaging the front of the building.

No one claimed responsibility for either attack, but bombings are common on the Mediterranean resort island where separatist groups have waged a two-decade campaign for greater autonomy from mainland France.

The outlawed Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC) Historic Wing recently stepped up its campaign following the detention of Francois Santoni, head of the Conculta Naziunalista, the FLNC's legal wing.
Santoni faces charges of attempted extortion and arms violations.
The FLNC traditionally carries out attacks on state facilities as well as "punitive" actions against businesses which refuse to pay "revolutionary taxes" to finance its activities.

The attacks followed a statement by the FLNC in Ajaccio claiming responsibility for the placing of a large bomb outside a post office in Marseille on the French mainland on Saturday which was defused before exploding.
The statement also claimed responsibility for a bomb blast which damaged the entrance to the law courts in the Corsican town of Corte early on Tuesday in which no one was hurt.
